segments: The seventeenth dynasty,
the Arab kings.
Before the Turks, they were completely unable to hold out,
but entered into their own interior lands.
And there remained those Armenians who had been appointed rulers by the Greeks,
fortifying themselves in mountains and rugged places.
In Cilicia, indeed,
[were] the two brothers, the sons of Constantine son of Roupen;
and in Gargar and Beth Bola, Michael and Johannes;
and in Kaysum, and in Ra'ban, and in Beth Hesne, and in the Roman Fortress, Kogh (or Kog?) Basil, that is, Basil the Thief;
and also in the district of Samosata, Constantine and Tabtug;
and also in Yastapor, the sons of Sanbel.
These were the territories that adhered to Kogh Basil, and to Dgha Basil, that is, the child Basil, whom the wife of Kogh Basil had brought up.
And Kurtig (or Kurdik?) was the administrator of this woman.
This was an evil man and a hater of the Syrians.
For he seized the Red Monastery, which is near Kaysum,
and gave it to Khrikorios (Grigorios?), Catholicos of the Armenians.
And the five monasteries of the house of the Qenaye, which are in the mountain of Zabar, he turned into villages.
And the fortress also of 'Arnish had been a monastery,
and Kurtig expelled the monks,
and placed in it soldiers and a garrison.
And he tormented the monks,
demanding from them two thousand dinars.
And Tancred, king of Antioch, fought against Kaysum for two years,
and was scarcely able to conquer it.
Because this Kurtig was very crafty,
the Franks were completely unable to overcome him,
until they devised a scheme and gave him a Frankish woman, just as the Philistines also [did] to Samson;
and that Frankish woman, whose name was Calamaria, killed him with poison.
Now, the wife of Kogh Basil,
when she saw the army of the Turks who had entered her country and were devastating [it],
sent to Aqsunqur, the emir of Khabur,
and promised him love and assistance.
And he sent an envoy to her, a man named Sunqur Draz, that is, 'the Long'.
And she sat upon a royal throne,
and stationed around her her noble handmaidens, adornment-clad.
And when Sunqur entered to her,
she set a throne for him before her,
and spoke with him craftily words of humility.
And while the Turks who were with Sunqur were encamped outside in tents, she said to him,
